summary.intent: Execute a handed-off 'pass-region' wave: run three parallel lanes (Opus, worktree isolation) to fix four GitHub issues (#2016, #2021, #1956, #2017), review and merge the resulting PRs, then write up the two ADRs the work implied.
summary.outcome: All three lanes completed and merged (PR 2059, 2060, 2063), closing all four issues with green CI and post-merge checks on main each time; cleaned up 37 stale placeholder branches; wrote and merged ADR 0054 and ADR 0055 as docs PRs (2081, 2082), resolved an index-table merge conflict from a concurrently merged ADR 0053, and flipped ADR 0054's status to Accepted at the user's request.

repo: Lane worktree pattern: launch fix lanes as background Opus agents with worktree isolation, draft PRs, and no CodeRabbit request; the orchestrator reviews the diff itself before spending the CodeRabbit slot
CodeRabbit review requests are rate-limited to one slot at a time across PRs, requiring sequential waits/monitors between requests

Lanes spawn their own nested 'Simplify review' sub-agents (simplification, reuse, efficiency, altitude axes) plus security/crypto-privacy/code reviews; results must be forwarded back to the lane to fold
AGENTS.md has a 'no happy-path narration' comment rule that reviewers flag when violated

ADR quality gate has 3 criteria (not clear without context, hard to reverse, real trade-off); read-only rules that aren't durable shapes should be folded into a related durable-shape ADR item rather than standing alone
ADR acceptance process: owner accepts by merging with status changed to 'Accepted on <date>' in both the status line and index row
Docs PRs use `@coderabbitai ignore` and carry no attribution lines
Squash-merging one ADR PR while a sibling ADR PR also edits the index table forces a rebase + re-insert of that PR's index row
Background Bash tool calls have a 10-minute cap; waits longer than that must be relaunched as detached processes or Monitor watchers

code.finding: staleness_now took borrow_mut on every read just to write 'reported', creating read-side effects; later fixed via SyncStatus::observe recording reads without pass-start events
run_past_deadline hand-wrote a poll_fn race that duplicated the existing within() combinator in record_plane.rs:153

refuse_below_cut_floor duplicated the cut-floor check already in RootPublish::check_publishable (net/rotation.rs:2215) — ended up existing in three hand-written copies with two different verdict mappings

Retire ledger entries began storing whole root blocks (up to 2MB) instead of just CIDs, breaking the ledger's 'three orders of magnitude smaller than CID set' design goal; fixed with a versioned entry grammar in ADR 0054
live_owing_record's Edit rule only compared head CID, missing that a later publish could reuse the same sequence number — the core loss-path bug fixed by adding an acknowledged-sequence mark

workflow: Forward nested sub-agent review results to the parent lane only after all four axes (simplification/reuse/efficiency/altitude) arrive, rather than one at a time, so the lane folds everything in one pass
When a lane agent dies mid-task (e.g. hitting a session rate limit), resume it via SendMessage with the remaining steps once the limit resets, rather than restarting from scratch
Delete merged placeholder branches from removed agent worktrees, but verify unmerged ones against main's content (e.g. squash-merge history) before deleting them
Correct timezone/timestamp entries in memory files to UTC to avoid drift across sessions

friction: Lane C and Lane A stopped mid-task multiple times without a final report (after simplify pass, after security review), requiring the orchestrator to inspect worktree state and manually resume each time
Lane A was terminated by an Opus session rate limit ('hit your session limit, resets 8:20pm Europe/Berlin'), stalling PR 2063 for roughly 3 hours
Background Bash 10-minute timeout cap nearly caused the CodeRabbit slot-wait script to die before the floor opened, requiring a detached-process workaround
CodeRabbit review requests take a long time to complete (30+ min on PR 2063), requiring re-arming Monitor watchers after the first one expired

Two ADR docs PRs both needed to insert a row into the same ADR index table, causing repeated merge conflicts each time one was merged before the other, plus a conflict from a third concurrently-merged ADR (0053)
User had to point out ADR 0054 landed with status still 'Proposed' instead of 'Accepted' — an easy-to-miss process step
open_items: Issue #2065 filed: dropped version whose staged root is already gone leaves rows unjournaled — candidate design is a charge-time journal instead of release-time
Drain signs scope-root publishes without taking the write-epoch lease (documented rationale in PR 2063 body, per ADR 0041 E2) — flagged but not changed
blueprint/engine.md and CONTEXT.md line updates were handled via ADR 0055 but should be double-checked against final merged wording
PR 2082 (ADR 0055) still pending user merge as of end of transcript, with CI green and rebased onto post-2054 main
Accepted residuals in both ADRs (mark surviving rotation, mark key exposing node id, potential mark-write-failure loss) are documented as intentionally accepted, not fixed
